evidence: ReservationController.reserve: maps ReserveBody fields (new Date(body.from), body.hours, body.electric) to reserveSpot.reserve(...) and returns the receipt. This is request translation, which belongs to the presentation layer.
ReservationController.cancel: hands off to cancelReservation.cancel(id) and returns { cancelled: id }. This is response shaping, which belongs to the presentation layer.
ReserveBody interface: the shape of the transport payload, which fits an inbound HTTP adapter.
No business logic, persistence or infrastructure calls appear anywhere in the file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReservationController is a thin inbound presentation adapter. It does two things: it turns the request body into arguments for the use case (it parses `from` into a Date and passes plate, hours and electric through), and it shapes the response (`{ cancelled: id }`). Both are normal presentation work. It holds no business rules such as availability, pricing or validation policy. It does no persistence and has no framework logic that belongs elsewhere. It injects the concrete ReserveSpotService class instead of the ReserveSpot input port. That is a dependency-direction concern, and import direction and layer-dependency rules are out of scope for this rule.
